source.title: Traveling Waves Integrate Spatial Information Through Time

confidence_rationale: PREPRINT (arXiv 2502.06034, v1 2025-02-09, latest v4 2025-06-11 -- the thought cites v3, a version difference worth noting but not a discrepancy). Verified. This is the implementation-side evidence Q-103's notes flagged as unverified, and it holds up: convolutional recurrent networks trained to produce traveling waves in their hidden state propagate information across locally connected units, effectively expanding receptive fields for long-range encoding, and on visual semantic segmentation they substantially outperform local feedforward models and rival non-local U-Nets with fewer parameters. Supports Q-103's REPRESENTATIONAL branch in an artificial system: the wave carries spatial information through time rather than merely gating. Confidence 0.55 -- a clean, relevant result, discounted for preprint status, for being a vision-segmentation architecture rather than an inter-representation coupling field, and because outperforming a local feedforward baseline shows the wave is USEFUL, not that its trajectory carries structure that a content-only account could not.
failure_signatures: Q-103's representational branch predicts the coupling trajectory carries relational structure beyond the instantaneous content it gates. This architecture demonstrates a wave carrying spatial information through time -- but its comparison is against models with SMALLER effective receptive fields, so the result is also explainable as cheap long-range communication, which is the routing-only branch. The discriminator Q-103 needs is not run here.

The chip's note that the parameter saving comes 'at a speed cost' is consistent with the abstract's efficiency framing; a REE mechanism adopting waves for long-range integration would inherit that latency, which matters for any claim about the actionable-now state.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Convolutional recurrent networks that learn to produce traveling waves in their hidden state propagate wave-like activation across locally connected units, expanding effective receptive fields for long-range encoding and communication. On visual semantic segmentation requiring global spatial context they substantially outperform local feedforward models and rival non-local U-Net architectures with fewer parameters, with claimed efficiency and training-stability benefits.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-103 asks whether an authority/coupling field's trajectory carries relational structure or only sets eligibility and gain. This is the artificial-system demonstration that a wave can carry spatial structure through time and be functionally load-bearing -- the implementation evidence Q-103's notes cited and marked unverified pending this pull.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A vision architecture, not a model of coupling between representational subsystems; the wave here IS the computation substrate rather than a field modulating access between regions. The baseline comparison is against models with smaller effective receptive fields, so the result is equally readable as efficient long-range routing -- it does not discriminate Q-103's two branches. Preprint; the thought cites v3 while v4 is current.
mapping.source_context: Artificial neural networks; visual semantic segmentation requiring global context.

confidence_components.notes: Preprint with a clear, relevant result and named authors overlapping the biological review banked alongside. Mapping capped because the architecture does not instantiate the object Q-103 is about.
